summary: Matija Sosic demonstrates Mage, a GPT-powered full-stack web app generator that produced over 10,000 applications in its first month. The tool accepts a plain English app description and generates complete React, Node.js, Prisma, and Wasp applications that users can download, run locally, and deploy. Sosic attributes Mage's success to three factors: specialization exclusively in full-stack web apps, the Wasp framework's high-level declarative configuration that eliminates boilerplate, and automated error fixing before delivering results. The architecture works in stages. Step Zero generates predictable code such as config files, authentication, and CSS without calling GPT. A code agent then executes three phases: planning (identifying queries, actions, entities, and pages), code generation, and error fixing. Common errors such as import mismatches were addressed with simple heuristics handling 90% of cases without GPT involvement. Cost optimization proved critical. Typical apps require 2-3 minutes and 25,000-60,000 tokens, costing 10-20 cents. By using GPT-4 only for the creative planning stage and GPT-3.5 for implementation, costs dropped 10x compared to using GPT-4 throughout. A competing agent producing similar apps cost 80 cents to 10 dollars. Sosic positions Mage as a highly customized full-stack starter rather than a universal app generator. Pushing it beyond its comfort zone or providing too little detail both increase error rates. Future work includes a live debugging mode for interactive refinement and potential fine-tuning of LLMs for Wasp, though Wasp's readable syntax makes the benefit uncertain.

Three key reasons for performance: specialization in full-stack web apps only, Wasp's high-level framework reducing boilerplate, and automated error fixing before delivery.

sections.title: Introduction and Live Demo
sections.summary: Sosic introduces Mage and demonstrates generating a Todo app from a plain English description, showing the resulting React, Node.js, Prisma, and Wasp code, running it locally, creating tasks, and verifying database state.

sections.title: Why Mage Works Well
sections.summary: Three main reasons for Mage's performance: specialization only in full-stack web apps, use of the high-level Wasp framework to remove boilerplate, and automated error fixing before delivering results.

sections.title: Under the Hood: Architecture and Error Fixing
sections.summary: Step Zero generates predictable code without GPT. The code agent then runs planning, generation, and error-fixing phases. Common errors like import mismatches were addressed with heuristics handling 90% of cases, aided by Wasp's reduced code surface.

sections.title: Cost Analysis and Model Optimization
sections.summary: Typical apps cost 10-20 cents using 25,000-60,000 tokens in 2-3 minutes. Using GPT-4 only for planning and GPT-3.5 for implementation reduced costs 10x. A competing agent cost 80 cents to $10 for similar apps.

sections.title: Use Cases and Limitations
sections.summary: Mage serves as a highly customized full-stack starter rather than a universal app generator. Pushing complexity increases errors, while too little detail is counterproductive. Most users found it an easy way to kickstart apps with mainstream stacks.

sections.title: Future Work and Conclusion
sections.summary: Future plans include a live debugging mode for interactive changes and exploring fine-tuned LLMs for Wasp. Sosic encourages trying Mage and joining the Wasp Discord community.
